testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road, how should you alert other drivers?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This warns other drivers that you are there.

questions.question: When checking your tires, what should you avoid?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you know?

options.text: You can usually drive faster than a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never rely only on warning signals to tell you a train is coming. Never try to race a train across the tracks. If there are multiple tracks, check all of them in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Keep weight as low as possible in the trailer. Cargo placed high makes the vehicle more likely to tip over. Low cargo is more stable.

questions.question: If you do not know the area where you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk around the area first to see what is there.
Do not use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Wait to see how someone else backs up in that area.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around the area first to see what is there.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you do not know the area, get out and walk around first. This helps you know where it is safe to back up.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle going 55 mph in good conditions needs about ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle going 55 mph in good conditions needs about 450 feet to stop.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, how often must you check that it is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or three hours after that.

questions.question: What can affect how long it takes to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are going, how heavy your vehicle is, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) mean?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle plus its cargo.
The total weight of a vehicle without cargo.
The total weight of the cargo only.
The maximum weight a vehicle is allowed to carry.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle plus its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of the vehicle and everything loaded on it.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, air pressure moves the rods when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of the following should you NOT check?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: When checking tires, look for at least 4/32 inch of tread on front tires and 2/32 inch on other tires. Check that tires are not worn, cracked, or over-inflated. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do as the engine slows down?
questions.explanation: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch as the engine approaches idle speed.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids happen on slippery roads. Release the accelerator to stop the skid.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in air brake tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A message appears on the control panel.

questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles have a low-pressure warning light that turns on when tank pressure drops below 60 psi. On large buses, the warning may activate at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic light

questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors before each trip. Make sure any trailer is straight when adjusting mirrors.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, how do you follow the trailer's turn?

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turn the steering wheel harder in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to the desired turn direction. Once the trailer begins turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of blocking a load?

options.text: It is dangerous and should never be done.
It stops cargo from shifting during transport.
It is only used for liquid loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops cargo from shifting during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking keeps cargo from sliding during transport. Cargo shifting can make the vehicle difficult to steer and control.

questions.question: What vehicle must you use for a CDL driving test?

options.text: The same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
Any vehicle, even if it is different from what you will drive.
A vehicle supplied by the testing station.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the driving test in the type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the test vehicle.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what air pressure must build up in both systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, the air compressor must build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: If you pull off to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Let your taillights warn other drivers.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off so you don't distract other drivers.
Keep your door open to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, always turn on your emergency flashers. This is very important at night. Taillights alone are not enough because other drivers might think your vehicle is moving normally and hit it.

questions.question: Before looking under your vehicle's hood, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake and/or chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake and/or chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Before checking under the hood, set the parking brake and/or place chock blocks under the wheels to keep the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: What happens if you don't pass the air brakes test?

options.text: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Your CDL will show an air brake restriction marked with an asterisk.
Your CDL will not be valid.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: If you do not pass the air brakes test, you will only be allowed to drive vehicles without air brakes.

questions.question: What can be in the air entering air storage tanks?
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you must:
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level correctly.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.explanation: After starting the engine during your pre-trip inspection, listen for any strange or unusual noises.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking your vehicle. The only exceptions are if your brakes are very hot or if your brakes are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: When entering a curve, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, slow down and downshift to a lower gear.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Which of the following crimes will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson will disqualify you from obtaining, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: How many driver licenses can you have?

options.text: An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another.
Two licenses: one for automobiles and one for trucks.

questions.explanation: You can only have one license. Having more than one is illegal and can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator and push in the clutch while shifting into neutral. Then release the clutch, let the vehicle reach the correct speed, push in the clutch again, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine compartment, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.explanation: When inspecting the engine compartment, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to its outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley parking area. Park in a straight position within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: In an emergency, if you must leave the roadway and drive on the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Steer so all wheels are on the shoulder.
Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: Keep one set of wheels on the pavement to maintain better control. Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops completely, then return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Create more space ahead of your vehicle to make it easier for the tailgating driver to pass. Driving faster is dangerous because the driver may continue tailgating at the higher speed, increasing the risk.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park in an area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Notify emergency services of your problem and your location.

questions.explanation: Leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not pull into a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Report the fire and your location to emergency services.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps provide additional control during hard braking. However, it does not necessarily reduce your stopping distance.

questions.question: If you feel tired before driving, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to reach your destination quickly.

questions.explanation: Caffeine and other stimulants will not make you more alert. They may keep you awake, but your body needs sleep. The only solution is to stop driving and get rest.

questions.question: How should a driver correct a drive-wheel braking skid?
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal first so the wheels can roll again. Then steer quickly in the direction you want to go. After that, steer back in the other direction to stop the skid.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up?

options.text: Back up as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk behind your vehicle to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your vehicle to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk the path behind your vehicle to look for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is acceptable?
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play should not exceed 10 degrees. This equals about 2 inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Why are roads very slippery when rain first starts to fall?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery at the start of rain. Water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface, creating a slick layer. As rain continues, the oil and grease wash away.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A device that warns of low air pressure.
A tube that sends air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that warns of low air pressure.
questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low air pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive very slowly?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, if local law allows.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you while driving a large vehicle, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: When being tailgated, slow down gradually and increase your following distance to let the other driver pass. Do not speed up. The driver may just tailgate you at the higher speed, making the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What is the correct use of turn signals while driving?

options.text: You do not need to signal your intentions.
Use signals only if a vehicle is next to you.
Do not signal if your lane change is obvious.
Always use turn signals to show others your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to show others your plans.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals to let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What should the front of an enclosed trailer have?
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in hot weather?

options.text: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, monitor tire pressure because air expands when heated. Keep enough oil in the engine and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system to prevent overheating. Antifreeze is important in both hot and cold weather.
